content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — capacity saturation detected in us-west-2 dedicated pool (pool-3). tokens/sec spiking, throttle events increasing, queue depth > 900. Paging @oncall-rotation and @eng-runtime

marta (eng-sre): acknowledged. I'm on it. pulling live metrics now. can someone confirm if this is customer-facing latency or internal backpressure?

marta (eng-sre): quick snapshot from datadog:
```
avg(tokens/sec)[5m] = 12k -> 48k
throttles/count[1m] = 0 -> 120
queue_depth.max = 920
latency.p95 = 520ms -> 2.1s
```

datadog-bot: dashboard snapshot: https://dd.example.com/dashboard/abcd1234 — shows tokens/sec and throttle spikes correlated at 15:02 UTC

kevin (eng-runtime): seeing model-specific pattern: most throttles coming from gptx-small-quant instances (hottest shard). My guess: autoscaler didn't react fast enough due to burst policy and min_capacity lock.

marta (eng-sre): starting live mitigation:
- enabling emergency capacity burst for pool-3 (+2 nodes)
- increasing request fallback to smaller model for high-latency routes

marta (eng-sre): running commands:
```bash
# reserve burst capacity immediately
redwood infra pool reserve --pool pool-3 --nodes 2 --reason "emergency scale - tokens/sec spike"
# flip fallback policy for prod-route-a to gptx-small-quant-lite
redwood config set routing.prod-route-a.fallback_model=gptx-small-quant-lite
```

infra-bot: accepted. scaling action queued — adding 2 nodes to pool-3. expected ready in ~70s.

marta (eng-sre): after applying burst: queue_depth dropped to ~300, throttles reduced to ~10/min, p95 latency down to ~600ms. customers still see some errors but much improved.

kevin (eng-runtime): good. we should also tune alerts — current queue_depth alert triggers at 500 which caused noise in previous incidents but here it tripped late. propose: switch to combination of queue_depth > 800 AND tokens/sec 5m avg > 30k, and add throttle_rate > 20/min as an escape hatch.

sophia (eng-platform): +1. Also add per-model throttle alerts — the aggregate hides hotspots. We should create a new dashboard tile for tokens/sec per model and per-shard so oncall can triage faster.

marta (eng-sre): putting proposed alert changes here for review: 
```yaml
- alert_name: capacity_saturation_combined
  expr: |
    (max_over_time(queue_depth[2m]) > 800 and avg_over_time(tokens_per_sec[5m]) > 30000)
    OR rate(throttle_events[2m]) > 20
  for: 2m
  severity: P2
  notify: # oncall + eng-runtime
    - channel: #pager-duty
- alert_name: per_model_throttle_high
  expr: rate(throttle_events{model=~"gptx-.*"}[3m]) > 5
  for: 1m
  severity: P3
  notify:
    - channel: #eng-sre
```

kevin (eng-runtime): that looks good. couple of tweaks: lower the for: to 1m for the escape hatch path so we can page faster on sudden throttle surges. keep the combined rule at 2m to avoid flapping.

marta (eng-sre): updated in place. I'll open a PR to change Datadog monitors and add the per-model widgets.

sophia (eng-platform): can we also add a synthetic load to validate scaling behavior? schedule a controlled spike against pool-3 after hours and observe autoscaler reaction and alert firing. capture perf baseline.

marta (eng-sre): yes — plan: run load test 03/18 02:00 UTC (low traffic), target tokens/sec ~50k for 10 mins, then ramp down. I'll create runbook steps in the PR.

kevin (eng-runtime): one more operational note — the autoscaler currently uses queue_depth threshold of 500 for ramp decisions. we should change autoscaler policy to consider tokens/sec and recent throttle rate in decision matrix. filing infra ticket INF-1129.

marta (eng-sre): filed INF-1129 and linked to this thread. PR for monitor changes: https://git.example.com/redwood/monitors/pulls/278 (contains dashboards and monitor JSON).

oncall-rotation: thanks team — I'm stepping off rotation, handing over to marta for the remainder of the incident follow-ups.

marta (eng-sre): will own post-incident actions: 1) update monitors 2) add per-model dashboard tiles 3) schedule spike test 4) postmortem doc in #postmortems with impact and customer list.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident marked RESOLVED at 1759002805 — service recovered to baseline after emergency capacity burst and fallback model routing. Follow-ups assigned: monitors PR 278, infra INF-1129, load test scheduled.

kevin (eng-runtime): noting customer impact: a subset of heavy-traffic customers experienced elevated latency and a small number (~12) of throttled requests between 15:01–15:08 UTC. ops will reach out if any customer escalations.

sophia (eng-platform): thanks all. feel free to add any extra notes to the postmortem — especially any assumptions the autoscaler made that we should document.

marta (eng-sre): adding final notes in postmortem: root cause = bursty tokens/sec from long-generation jobs on single hot shard + autoscaler decision lag because of min_capacity lock and single-metric scaling. remediation: combine tokens/sec and throttle metrics in alerts and autoscaler, add per-model monitoring, increase autoscaler sensitivity for short bursts, and create runbook for emergency capacity bursts.

marta (eng-sre): closing thread — follow-ups tracked in PR/INF tickets above. :thumbsup:
